title: PS-22 Repeated low-dose endotoxin exposure on hematological and febrile response in nulliparous Rambouillet ewes
content:
Abstract
Administration of bacterial endotoxin, lipopolysaccharide (LPS), elicits immune response that can adversely affect female fertility and subsequent lamb performance. Nulliparous ewes are immunologically naïve due to limited exposure to common pathogens encountered during copulation, gestation, and parturition. The objective of this study was to evaluate the impact of repeated administration of low-dose LPS in nulliparous ewes during key stages of folliculogenesis on febrile and hematologic immune response. Fourteen Rambouillet ewes (age 9 mo; 56.4 ± 1.5 kg) were stratified by body weight (BW) and assigned to receive subcutaneous injections of saline (CON, n = 4), 1.5 µg/kg BW LPS (LOW, n = 5), or 3.0 µg/kg BW LPS (HIGH, n = 5) on d 5, 10, and 15 of a synchronized estrous cycle. Whole blood for complete blood count was collected via jugular venipuncture on d 5, 10, and 15 at h 0, 2, 4, 12, and 24 relative to LPS challenge. Rectal temperature and behavioral observations were recorded prior to and after LPS challenge at regular intervals to assess immune response. Data were analyzed as a split plot design using the mixed procedure of SAS. Prior to LPS injection, rectal temperatures on d 5 were similar among treatments but increased in LOW and HIGH LPS-treated ewes by 4 h compared with CON (41.2°C vs. 39.1°C; P < 0.05). Subsequent LPS challenge days demonstrated parallel but muted febrile responses. On d 5 and 15, circulating total white blood cells (TWBC) tended to decrease at 4 h in HIGH ewes compared to LOW and CON (P ≤ 0.10). However, by 24 h TWBC were markedly elevated in LOW and HIGH treatment groups compared with CON (P < 0.05). Additionally, TWBC and lymphocytes were initially elevated (P < 0.05) on d 10 prior to LPS administration at 0 h in HIGH LPS-treated ewes compared to CON, suggesting a carry-over response from the initial challenge on d 5. On d 10 and 15, LOW and HIGH LPS-treated ewes demonstrated elevated (P < 0.05) immune cell populations at 12 and 24 h compared to CON. On d 15, neutrophils were elevated by 4 h in LOW (P = 0.09) and HIGH (P < 0.05) compared to CON. Hematological parameters were slightly elevated in LOW LPS-treated ewes compared to HIGH and CON on d 5. No change in red blood cell parameters were noted on d 10 or 15. These data demonstrate that repeated low-dose endotoxin administration induces hematological alterations in immunologically naïve ewes. Unappreciated hematologic immune changes associated with endotoxin exposure could ultimately contribute to decreased reproductive efficiency.
